sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Mount Holly along Main Street (today's High Street), drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Main Street runs down the left third of the sheet from Water Street and Garden Street at the top to Washington Street at the lower left, lined on both sides with brick and frame stores of two and three storeys: the Mt. Holly Opera House (moving pictures), a newspaper plant, an auto garage and repair shop, the Y.M.C.A., the Union National Bank (built 1927), the Farmers Trust Co. and a hardware and paint store. Brainard Street crosses the top of the area and Murrell Street, a narrow side street with the Post Office, crosses a little below it. Paxson Street, a narrow street with a 4 inch water pipe, runs down the middle of the sheet to Mill Street, where the street is lined with brick stores and a garage with a vulcanizing shop. A branch of Rancocas Creek crosses the lower part of the sheet from White Street toward Pine Street, with Church Street along the bottom edge and a row of dwellings between the creek and Church Street. Buttonwood Run enters at the right and runs toward the middle. The right side holds frame dwellings with outbuildings and a large brick building on the upper right. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are lettered along each street, and the margins carry the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 3, 4, 6, 8 and 13. A scale bar is printed in the bottom street and a compass rose in the top margin.
notes: Main Street is today's High Street (OpenStreetMap), Brainard is today's Brainerd Street.
Murrell Street, Paxson Street and Mill Street junctions were hand-picked because they are drawn narrow or at a fork and the detector missed or misplaced them; fit is medium confidence.

Downtown: Main (High Street), Brainard (Brainerd St), Murrell, Paxson, Mill, Washington, White, Church, Pine; Rancocas Creek and its branch, Buttonwood Run. 50 ft, drawn with north up. One part; five junctions hand-picked (detector paired block lines and narrow alleys).

sheet-3-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 3 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. It covers the area between Pearl Street at the top and Wall Street at the bottom, from Pine Street on the west to Cherry and Green Streets on the east, crossed diagonally by Mill Street. Brainard Street enters from the upper left and ends at Buttonwood Street, which runs north to south through the middle of the sheet. Two watercourses cross it: Buttonwood Run, flowing west to east above Mill Street, and a branch of Rancocas Creek in the lower half, below Mill Street. The Mt. Holly High School, a large brick building with steam heat, stands on Brainard Street. Along Mill Street are the Mill St. Hotel, apartments, brick and frame dwellings, an agricultural implements warehouse and blacksmith shop near Buttonwood, an auto repair shop, an office of the water company, a plumbers' storehouse at Pine Street, and a canoe storage and repair shop by the creek branch. Pine Street, lined with dwellings, carries the Relief Fire Company house near Church Street and an auto delivery yard with a stable behind it. Much of the land between the creek branch and the Cherry Street blocks is open. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along every street. The lower right corner of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Brainard is today's Brainerd Street in OpenStreetMap.
Fitted scale about 2 percent smaller than sheet 9; residuals of 2 to 4 m are spread over the sheet.
Four junctions (Mill/Pine, Mill/Buttonwood, Mill/Cherry, Pearl/Cherry) were hand-picked; Green/Mill was left out (about 6 m off the fit).

Buttonwood, Pearl, Brainard (Brainerd St), Mill, Green, Pine, Church, Wall, Buttonwood Run and branch of Rancocas Creek. 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset lower right (Pine and Wall south to Nassau Pl, drawn with north nearly up).

sheet-3-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 3 is an inset in the lower right corner, set off by a heavy border and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up, at a different angle from the main map. It shows the block south of Wall Street and east of Pine Street, running south to Nassau Place, a short lane marked as an arbitrary name, and east to the bank of Rancocas Creek, which curves along the right side of the inset. The area above Wall Street is blank and marked as belonging to the main part of the sheet. Pine Street, 60 feet wide with 8-inch and 3-inch water pipes, forms the west edge. The frontage on Wall Street carries a row of small two-storey frame dwellings, numbered from 20 to 112, with two brick dwellings at the Pine Street corner; behind them are sheds, storehouses, coops and auto garages. Pine Street frontage is lined with dwellings numbered 37 to 49. The block is cut by lot lines running from Wall Street toward Nassau Place; the land toward the creek is open. A small north arrow sits in the upper right of the inset, and the scale bar of the sheet is printed along its lower edge, with the adjoining sheet numbers 4 and 17 in the margins.
notes: Nassau Place is marked as an arbitrary name on the sheet and is not in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from two points: Pine/Wall detected, and the corner of Pine and Nassau Place carried from sheet 17; low confidence.

Buttonwood, Pearl, Brainard (Brainerd St), Mill, Green, Pine, Church, Wall, Buttonwood Run and branch of Rancocas Creek. 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset lower right (Pine and Wall south to Nassau Pl, drawn with north nearly up).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers a largely open block south of the town centre, bounded by Church Street at the top, White Street on the left, Pine Street on the right and Monroe Street across the lower middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and the sheet is turned about ten degrees, with north to the upper right. A row of frame dwellings and a milk depot lines the south side of Church Street, with a large garage, storage sheds and a lumber or building-supply yard behind it. Most of the interior is vacant or garden land crossed only by lot lines, with a few scattered dwellings along White Street. A second row of dwellings, some pink brick, faces Pine Street on the right, from Church Street down to the Rancocas Creek bridge near the bottom right corner, where a wooden bridge is lettered. South of Monroe Street the land is almost entirely blank, with a few small dwellings and sheds at the left edge. The Rancocas Creek curves in a large loop across the lower part of the sheet and runs off the bottom edge. Street widths of 37 and 60 feet are lettered, with water pipes of 3, 4 and 8 inches along White, Church, Monroe and Pine Streets. A compass rose and a north arrow stand in the middle and the scale bar is printed in the lower left. The margins give the neighbouring sheets as 2, 3, 5, 16 and 17.
notes: Monroe is today's East Monroe Street (OpenStreetMap); Charles Street and Church Street share one junction with White Street today.
Church/Pine and Pine/Wall junctions at the right edge were hand-picked from the drawn Pine Street width, not detected.
Rancocas Creek bridge at the bottom right is lettered 'Wooden Bridge'.
Church, White, Pine, Monroe (East Monroe St), Budd, Wall; Rancocas Creek loop. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district on the west side of Mount Holly south of the town centre, bounded by Charles Street along the top, Bispham Street through the left middle, White Street on the right and Monroe Street along the lower edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the sheet turned about ten degrees so that north points toward the upper right. Rows of frame dwellings with sheds and stables fill the blocks between Beaupel Place, Bispham Street and White Street, and are numbered along each frontage with Budd Street crossing the middle. The Burlington County Road Department occupies a block near the top, with a garage, sheds and a carpenter's shop. At the left edge, beside the Pennsylvania Railroad's Mt. Holly and Burlington Branch, stand the Charles E. Rogers feed mill (custom grinding) with its storage house, a range of vacant and dilapidated sheds, and the coal yard of Akins & Son. Rancocas Creek runs down the far left margin. A second line of dwellings faces Monroe Street below the main blocks, and the area south of Monroe Street is blank apart from a few sheds and dwellings near White Street. Alleys 15 feet wide divide the blocks, and street widths of 35 to 50 feet are lettered. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Bispham, Monroe and White Streets. A compass rose stands at the right edge, a dash-dot match line is lettered A and B at the lower right, and the scale bar is at the foot. The margins name sheets 4 and 6.
notes: Monroe is today's East Monroe Street and West Monroe Street (OpenStreetMap) on either side of White Street.
Beaupel Place has no OpenStreetMap name of its own; no junction on it was used.
Budd Street west of Bispham Street is named West Read Street in OpenStreetMap.
Charles, Bispham, Beaupel Place (not in OSM), Budd (West Read Street west of Bispham), Monroe, White; P.R.R. branch at left. 50 ft. One part; no control east of White.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the loop of the Rancocas Creek on the west side of central Mount Holly, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned about nine degrees so that north points toward the upper right. Water Street runs along the top of the sheet, with a row of shops and works on its south side: E. H. Stokes coal and wood with a trestle, the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey electric sub-station, upholsterer, auto trimming and repairing, a machine shop and a junk yard. Washington Street crosses the lower half from the railroad at the left to the Iron Bridge over the creek near White Street on the right, lined with dwellings, an auto sales and service garage, a photographer, and the Fire Department Union Hose Co. No. 2. Beside the bridge on White Street is the Police Station. The creek curves around a large open area lettered Athletic Field, which holds a grand stand, bleachers, booths and, on its east side, a dance hall and a store house. A second arc of the creek crosses below Washington Street, and Charles Street runs along the bottom edge with small outbuildings on its north side. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Mt. Holly and Burlington Branch runs down the left edge. Street widths of 50 and 55 feet and 8 inch water pipes are lettered on Washington Street, and hydrants stand at the corners. A compass rose with a north arrow stands in the middle of the field. The margins name the adjoining sheets 2, 5, 7 and 13. The fit is drawn about 2 percent under the 50 foot scale.
notes: Trinity Lane exists in OpenStreetMap near Washington Street but is not lettered on this sheet.
Water Street on the north bank is probably today's Rancocas Road; no junction on it was used.
Charles/Church/White and Washington/White were hand-picked from the drawn White Street centre (water pipe); the detector put the first one on White's west edge.

Rancocas Creek loop, Athletic Field, Water (Rancocas Road), Washington, Bispham, Charles, White. 50 ft, fitted about 7.77 px/ft. One part; Trinity Lane removed by the lead (not drawn; detector fitted lot lines).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the industrial belt on the west side of Mount Holly along King Street and the Rancocas Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned about ten degrees so that north points toward the upper right. King Street runs diagonally from Water Street at the top to Washington Street near the bottom, crossing the creek on a concrete bridge. North of the creek, on the west side of King Street, stand the Tri-State Passenger Lines auto bus garage and the Wm. Horstmann and Co. knitting mill with the S. L. Kimmelman garment factory; on the east side is the French Lumber Co. yard with its lumber sheds. South of the creek a very large yarn and hosiery mill with dyeing, storage and boiler buildings, a reinforced concrete extension built in 1921 and tanks with sprinklers, fills the block west of King Street. East of King Street are a lumber storage works, an auto sales and service garage, the Imperial Hotel on Washington Street and the coal and wood yard of S. B. Lippincott with coal bins and a lime shed, served by the Pennsylvania Railroad's Mt. Holly and Burlington Branch at the right. At the bottom right are the Mt. Holly Textile Co., a china and glassware warehouse and the Sinclair Refining Co. oil depot, beside a loop of the creek crossed by a wooden bridge. Madison Avenue leaves Washington Street to the south-west with a block of small dwellings and a boarding house. Reimer Street and Arch Street, with dwellings, lie at the left edge. Mt. Holly Laundry is at the upper right. Hydrants, water pipes and watchman notes are lettered throughout. The margins name sheets 6, 13, 14, 22 and 24.
notes: Water Street here is today's Rancocas Road (OpenStreetMap): King Street / Rancocas Road is the junction used.
Arch/Reimer was hand-picked. Only four control points; none in the eastern half, so the east side rests on scale and rotation.
A concrete bridge carries King Street over the creek and a wooden bridge crosses the loop at the lower right.

King Street industrial belt (Ancocas hosiery mills, Kimmelman garment factory, French Lumber Co.), Water (Rancocas Road), Washington, Madison Av, Arch, Reimer. 50 ft. One part; no control in the east half.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northern end of Mount Holly's town centre between Main or High Street on the left and Buttonwood Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned about twenty-six degrees so that north points toward the upper left. Union Street runs along the top and Garden Street crosses the middle, while Brainard Street cuts diagonally across the lower left and bottom of the sheet. The upper blocks hold frame dwellings, with apartments, offices and brick stores on the High Street frontage, St. Andrew's Protestant Episcopal Church with its Parish House, the First Baptist Church, the Friends Meeting House and a Knights of Pythias hall. Maple Leaf Cottage, a boarding house, stands near Garden Street. The lower blocks include the New Jersey Bell Telephone Co. and the Mt. Holly National Bank near High Street, a long shed, the Methodist Episcopal Church, a music school and a row of dwellings along Brainard Street, and at the bottom right the large brick Mt. Holly Public School with its School Annex and a kindergarten. The middle of the northern blocks is open yard land with outbuildings and stables, crossed by alleys and lot lines. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches and hydrants are marked along each street, with street widths such as 33, 35 and 40 feet. A compass rose is at the upper left and the scale bar at the lower left. The margins name the adjoining sheets 2, 3, 9, 12 and 13. Water Street enters from the left at Garden Street.
notes: Main or High is today's High Street, Brainard is Brainerd Street and Water Street is Rancocas Road (OpenStreetMap).
The Garden / High / Rancocas Road junction was rejected by the first pass (10.9 m from the fit): the old Water Street meets High Street north of where Garden meets it.
All six fitted points carry 2 to 3 m residuals; the sheet may be slightly irregular.
Union, Garden, Main or High, Buttonwood, Brainard, Pearl; Mt. Holly Public School. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers four residential blocks on the north side of central Mount Holly, bounded by Union Street at the top, Pearl Street at the bottom, Buttonwood Street on the west and Mt. Holly (today's Mount Holly Avenue) on the east, with Garden Street crossing the middle and Cherry Street running north to south through the centre. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the upper right. The blocks are lined with two- and three-storey frame dwellings, most with rear sheds, stables and auto garages, and a number of brick houses along Garden Street east of Cherry. The largest buildings are the First Presbyterian Church with its Sunday school on the north side of Garden Street west of Cherry, drawn in stone and brick with steam heat and electric and gas lighting. Commercial and public uses are few: the Holly Dairy Co. milk depot on Buttonwood Street, a second milk depot behind the houses on the south side of Garden Street, the Central Greenhouses near Cherry Street, and the Good Intent Fire Company house at the corner of Buttonwood and Garden. Water pipes of 3 to 12 inches are drawn along every street, with fire hydrants and their positions marked at the corners, and street widths of 40 to 50 feet are lettered. House numbers run along each frontage. The margins name the adjoining sheets 8, 10, 11, 12 and 3.
notes: Mt. Holly is today's Mount Holly Avenue.
The detector paired a line south of Pearl at Buttonwood; that junction was hand-picked.
Union, Garden, Pearl, Buttonwood, Cherry, Mt. Holly (Mount Holly Avenue). 50 ft. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the blocks on the north side of central Mount Holly between Broad Street at the top and Garden Street at the bottom, with Mt. Holly (today's Mount Holly Avenue) on the left and Clover Street on the right. Union Street crosses the sheet on a slight diagonal and meets Jacksonville Road at the upper right, where the road leaves the sheet to the northeast. Risdon Street runs through the middle of the sheet from Union Street to Garden Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is mostly residential: rows of two-storey frame dwellings with sheds and auto garages line Mt. Holly and the west side of Risdon Street, and a few dwellings stand along Garden Street and Clover Street. The largest works are the Jenoff, Landy and Co. garment factory on the north side of Union Street, drawn in pink with its watchman, steam heat and electric light legend, and a second brick building, an auto house and storage, beside it. Browne and Phares, manufacturers of antique furniture reproductions, occupy a long building between Mt. Holly and Risdon Street, with a lumber shed and a Boy Scout Hall nearby. A contractor's yard with lumber storage lies behind the houses on Risdon Street, and its large open block, with the compass rose, is numbered 207. A milk depot stands on Garden Street. Street widths of 20 to 70 feet are lettered, and water pipes of 2 to 8 inches are drawn in the streets. The margins give the adjoining sheets 9, 11 and 12.
notes: Mt. Holly is today's Mount Holly Avenue.

The junction of Union Street, Clover Street and Jacksonville Road is flared and was left out of the fit; the detector put it about 17 ft off and a hand pick disagreed with the other points by about 4 m.
Union, Garden, Mt. Holly Av, Clover, Risdon, Broad, Jacksonville Rd. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the eastern part of Mount Holly at 100 feet to an inch, from Garden Street at the top to Rancocas Creek at the bottom. Mill Street runs across the sheet from Cherry Street in the west, past the Mt. Holly crossing, to a junction with Branch Street, then continues south-east as East Mill Street. Branch Street runs north-east from that junction to the top right corner, past Elm, Maple, Walnut, Moore Drive, Cripp's Drive and Newcomb Drive. Green Street follows the creek in the south and crosses Top E Toy Street, Mifflin Street and Arnold Street. The northern part holds scattered frame dwellings along Garden Street and Mt. Holly and the Woolman Street block; the town's main street frontage on Mill Street is a continuous row of dwellings. Button Wood Run enters from the west and flows into a long lake, shown in blue, whose south shore carries Lake Drive. Rancocas Creek, with a pond and a small island, crosses the bottom left. The Mt. Holly Water Co. pumping station, with a sedimentation basin and filter, stands on Green Street, with contractors' supply works beside it. The sheet's east side is mostly vacant blocks numbered 174 to 180 and 311 to 312, with few buildings. The margins give the adjoining sheets 3, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 13.
notes: Elm Street is drawn between Garden and Branch Streets; the fit places it on today's Girard Street (medium confidence).
Newcomb Drive is today's Newcombe Drive; Cripp's Drive is today's Cripps Drive.
Mill Street and East Mill Street are both Mill Street today.
The Cherry Street and Pearl Street junction was left out of the fit (5 m off).

East side: Garden, Mill, E. Mill, Branch, Green, Arnold, Mifflin, Top E Toy, Woolman, Elm (modern Girard Street, medium confidence), Walnut, Maple St., Newcomb Drive, Cripp's Drive, Moore Drive, Lake Drive; Rancocas Creek, Lake, Mt. Holly Water Co. pumping station. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 12 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. It covers the northern residential district between Main or High Street on the west and Mt. Holly (Mount Holly Avenue) on the east, from Union Street at the bottom up to Hillside Road (Rossell) and Prospect Street at the top. Between them run Buttonwood Street, Mt. View Avenue and Cherry Street, crossed by Ridgeway and Broad Streets and by a short Rossell Street; Langstaff runs north from Hillside Road. Bartram Avenue and Grant Street meet High Street from the west. The blocks are mostly two-storey frame dwellings with garages, with brick houses along Broad Street and High Street. Near Union and High Street stands the library. The large tract east of Cherry Street and north of Ridgeway is Mt. Holly Cemetery, with cemetery sheds, left largely blank. Several blocks in the upper part are only partly built, with open lots. Water pipes up to 12 inches run along the streets, including a 12-inch main to the reservoir on Prospect Street. Street widths of 40 to 70 feet are lettered. The upper right corner of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2) and the margins name sheets 8, 9, 10, 13 and 16.
notes: Main or High is today's High Street; Mt. Holly is Mount Holly Avenue; Hillside Rd (Rossell) is Hillside Road.

North side: Main or High, Hillside Rd (Rossell), Langstaff, Rossell, Mt. View Av, Cherry, Ridgeway, Broad, Union, Buttonwood, Mt. Holly; Mt. Holly Cemetery. 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset upper right (Ridgeway and Broad east of Mt. Holly Av to Jacksonville Rd).

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 is an inset in the upper right corner, set off by a heavy border and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the two blocks east of Mt. Holly (Mount Holly Avenue) between Ridgeway Street at the top and Broad Street at the bottom, running east to Jacksonville Road, which cuts across the right end of the inset on a diagonal. A short street parallel to Ridgeway in the middle of the blocks is marked as not opened. North of Ridgeway the ground is part of Mt. Holly Cemetery, drawn mostly blank with a few dwellings and sheds along the road. The blocks hold rows of small two-storey frame dwellings with house numbers from 301 to 360, many with auto garages at the rear, and some vacant lots toward Jacksonville Road. Six- and eight-inch water pipes run along Ridgeway and Broad Streets with hydrants at the corners, and the widths of the streets (50 to 70 feet) and of Jacksonville Road (60 feet) are lettered. The sheet number of the adjoining sheet 10 is printed below Broad Street.
notes: The two Jacksonville Road junctions were hand-picked; the detector did not resolve the acute angles.
Mt. Holly is today's Mount Holly Avenue.

North side: Main or High, Hillside Rd (Rossell), Langstaff, Rossell, Mt. View Av, Cherry, Ridgeway, Broad, Union, Buttonwood, Mt. Holly; Mt. Holly Cemetery. 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset upper right (Ridgeway and Broad east of Mt. Holly Av to Jacksonville Rd).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north-western part of Mount Holly at 100 feet to an inch, with High Street (printed Main or High) along the right edge. Bartram Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from High Street to the west, with Thorndyke, Berwick, Rutland and Clifton Avenues running south from it. Grant Street crosses the lower part, with Brown Street and King Street meeting it on the west, and Kearney Street and Water Street run along the bottom. The Mt. Holly and Burlington branch of the Pennsylvania Railroad runs diagonally from the lower left to the top right beside Clifton Avenue. On High Street, from Hillside Road at the top down to Union Street, the frontage has a series of larger buildings in pink, and the sheet shows the Burlington County Court House and the Hall of Records, the County Jail with its walled yard, the Armory of Co. M 114th Infantry, the Elks Home and the New Washington hotel. Other large buildings are the Samuel Miller Public School on Clifton Avenue, the Fenimore Brothers grist mill and the Hollyford Ice and Cold Storage Co. beside the railroad, a Seventh Day Adventist church on Grant Street, and the Weaver Manufacturing Co. Block numbers 154 to 156, 210 and 211 mark open land and long lots on the west side. A compass rose and a dash-dot match line A-B appear at left. The margins give the adjoining sheets 2, 6, 7, 8, 12, 14 and 16.
notes: Water Street is probably today's Rancocas Road.
Main or High is today's High Street.

The Bartram Avenue junctions are 4 to 6 m off the other control and were left out; the Grant Street and Brown Street group is consistent with itself but 2 percent larger in scale than the High Street points, so the fit is weak (RMSE about 3.7 m).
Kearney Street and Berwick Avenue are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

Northwest: Main or High, Water (Rancocas Road), Grant, Kearney, King, Brown, Clifton, Rutland, Thorndyke, Berwick, Bartram; county court house, jail, armory, P.R.R. 100 ft. One part; weak fit (Bartram junctions left out).

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the west side of Mount Holly at 100 feet to an inch. The upper right of the sheet is Water Street, running south-east along the north bank of Rancocas Creek from Brown Street, with a row of dwellings along its south side and a few larger works: the Burlington County Shoe Co. and J. Budd Woolston's flour blending plant. The creek crosses the sheet from the top left to the right edge. The lower left holds the main residential district west of the town centre, laid out along Washington Street, which runs across the sheet to King Street and Madison Avenue at the right. Arch Street and Chestnut Street run parallel to it on the north. Carlton Avenue, Willow Street, Rose Street, Oak Street, Raphael Street and Reimer Street run across it, with Filbert Street and Holeman Street at the bottom left. Churches include St. Paul M. E. Church and the Roman Catholic Church of the Sacred Heart on Washington Street. The Samuel Aaron School (colored) stands at the left on Chestnut Street. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Toms River Branch crosses the lower right in a spread of tracks with a freight house, sheds and the Mt. Holly passenger station near Madison Avenue. The sheet is drawn with the street grid turned about 13 degrees from the page. Block numbers 104, 105, 106, 162, 20, 21 and 23 are printed, and the margins give the adjoining sheets 7, 13, 15 and 16.
notes: Water Street is probably today's Rancocas Road.

Arch Street and Filbert Street are drawn closer to Washington Street than today's centrelines, and Rose Street and Oak Street junctions are 5 to 10 m off the Washington Street group; all were left out of the fit.
The fit rests on four junctions along Washington Street and one at Brown and Water Street, so its cross-street scale is weak.
Raphael Street is printed in parentheses.

West: Water (Rancocas Road), Brown, Washington, Chestnut, Arch, Rose, Oak (Raphael St.), Reimer, Willow, Filbert, Carlton Av, Madison Av, King St; Rancocas Creek, P.R.R. Toms River branch and Mt. Holly passenger station. 100 ft. One part; low control (Arch, Filbert, Rose, Oak left out).

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 15 is the main map of Clermont, the western end of Mount Holly on the line between Hainesport and Northampton Townships, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Washington Street runs diagonally across the upper half, with 1st St. above it and the cross streets Cumberland, Middlesex and Hunderton below; further east are Carlton Avenue, Holeman Street and Carlton Ct. The township line between Hainesport and Northampton is drawn through the middle. The blocks of Clermont are filled with small frame dwellings and a garage. The main industry is the Royle & Pilkington Co., makers of tapestry goods, a large brick and frame mill on Holeman Street with its engine and boiler houses, a reservoir and a long note on its watchman, heating, power and sprinklers. North of Washington Street stand the Northampton Textile Co. weaving mill on an unnamed road and the 2nd Baptist Church (colored) on Carlton Avenue. The P.R.R. Toms River Branch crosses the lower part of the sheet with a siding curving off it, and the Rem Co. cement block works lie south of the tracks. In the lower right a separate group of blocks on Ridge Avenue, Caley Avenue, Carlton Avenue (not opened) and Cedar Street is drawn, crossed by the Lumberton and Northampton Township line. The lower left corner holds an inset (part 2).
notes: Hunderton is today's Hunterdon Avenue (North Hunterdon Avenue north of Washington).
Cumberland is North and South Cumberland Avenue; Middlesex is Middlesex Avenue.
Carlton Avenue in the lower right and Cedar are marked as not opened.

Clermont (west end): Washington, 1st St, Cumberland, Middlesex, Hunderton, Holeman, Carlton Av, Ridge Av, Caley Av; Royle & Pilkington Co. 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset lower left (Washington, Maple Av, Cumberland, Brotherhood Cemetery).

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 15 is an inset in the lower left corner, set off by a heavy border and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, at about the same angle as the main map. It continues Clermont westward along Washington Street, from Cumberland at its right edge to the west beyond Maple Avenue. North of Washington Street the block marked 158 holds a few scattered two-storey frame dwellings and a hen house, and is lettered Clermont. South of Washington Street lies the Brotherhood Cemetery, a large open tract drawn blank, and between Maple Avenue and Cumberland a block with a Lutheran parsonage, dwellings and a large brick garage with auto repair shop. Eight-inch and six-inch water pipes run along Washington Street, Maple Avenue and Cumberland, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered. House numbers along Washington Street run from 605 to 613. The adjoining sheet is marked 15 on the right, where Cumberland continues on the main map of this sheet.
notes: Placed as a two-point helmert (Maple/Washington and Cumberland/Washington); low confidence away from Washington Street.

Clermont (west end): Washington, 1st St, Cumberland, Middlesex, Hunderton, Holeman, Carlton Av, Ridge Av, Caley Av; Royle & Pilkington Co. 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset lower left (Washington, Maple Av, Cumberland, Brotherhood Cemetery).

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 covers the southwest of Mount Holly, west of the heavy dividing line on the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. Its streets run north to south (Caley Avenue, Madison Avenue, Spout Spring Avenue and Greenwood Avenue) and are crossed by Cedar Street, Bank Avenue, Ridge Avenue, South Avenue (Dobbins Avenue) and Richmond Avenue. The line between Northampton and Lumberton Townships crosses the lower part of the sheet. The northern blocks along Madison Avenue are closely built with small two-storey frame dwellings; further south the lots are larger and many are vacant. The principal institution is the Burlington County Hospital, whose buildings stand on both sides of Madison Avenue: a large main building between Madison and Spout Spring Avenues, drawn with notes on its construction, heating and lighting, and a wing with a nurses' home west of Madison Avenue. A club house stands on Caley Avenue. The blocks south of Richmond Avenue and east of Greenwood Avenue are mostly empty. Water pipes of 3 to 8 inches run along the main streets with hydrants at the corners. The adjoining sheets 14 and 15 are named in the left margin and the scale bar is printed near the bottom.
notes: South Av. (Dobbins Av.) is today's West South Avenue.
Fitted scale about 5 percent smaller than the 100 ft nominal (as on sheet 17).

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 left (Caley, Madison, Spout Spring, Greenwood, Cedar, Bank, Ridge, South Av (Dobbins Av), Richmond; Burlington County Hospital); part 2 right, drawn at another angle (Mt. Holly Fair Association grounds, Main or High, Burlington Rd, Wood Lane, Front, Evergreen, Prospect).

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 lies east of the heavy dividing line on the sheet and is drawn at another angle, with its own north arrow pointing nearly straight up. It shows the grounds of the Mt. Holly Fair Association at the north end of town: an oval race track with a judges' stand, an old grand stand marked as dilapidated, a row of stables along the north and east edges, water closets, small sheds and two large exhibition buildings near the entrance. The grounds are bounded on the east by Wood Lane (Wood Pecker Lane) and on the southwest by Burlington Road, which forks from Main or High Street at a filling station. South of the fork, Main or High Street runs down the sheet with Front, Evergreen and Prospect Streets meeting it from the east; the blocks along it hold scattered two-storey frame and brick dwellings and a stone dwelling, with large vacant lots. A 12-inch water main to the reservoir runs along Prospect Street. The sheet numbers 12 and 13 are printed in the lower right where those sheets continue.
notes: Main or High is today's High Street; the old fork with Burlington Road and Wood Lane does not match the modern road layout.
Placed as a helmert from three junctions along High Street, two hand-picked; low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 left (Caley, Madison, Spout Spring, Greenwood, Cedar, Bank, Ridge, South Av (Dobbins Av), Richmond; Burlington County Hospital); part 2 right, drawn at another angle (Mt. Holly Fair Association grounds, Main or High, Burlington Rd, Wood Lane, Front, Evergreen, Prospect).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the south side of Mount Holly beyond Rancocas Creek, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Pine Street runs diagonally up the sheet from Pemberton Road and South Avenue at the bottom to Monroe Street and Nassau Place at the top, crossing Rancocas Creek on a bridge. The creek loops across the upper half, and a cemetery with a small chapel occupies the open ground west of Pine Street. East of Pine Street, Shreve and Hulme Streets run southeast in parallel, lined with small frame dwellings, and the Hill Construction Co. office and storehouse stands on Hulme Street. West of Pine Street are Herald Avenue, Harrison Avenue and Nippins Avenue with their dwellings and green houses. The P.R.R. line crosses the sheet from upper left to lower right, with the Burlington County Supply & Produce Co. warehouses and coal sheds beside it on Pine Street. At the bottom, near Pemberton Road, stand the Burlington County Children's Home, the Mary A. Dobbins Memorial Home with its dormitories, a school and a filling station. Large parts of the sheet are open land. Water pipes run along Pine Street and the streets east of it.
notes: Monroe St. is today's East Monroe Street; South Av. is East South Avenue; Pemberton Rd is South Pemberton Road.
Harrison Avenue junctions are drawn about 10 m from the modern street line; hand-picked and kept, with residuals of about 5 m.
Fitted scale about 4 percent smaller than the 100 ft nominal.
South: Pine, Herald, Harrison, Nippins, South Av, Pemberton Rd, Hulme, Shreve; Rancocas Creek; P.R.R. 100 ft. One part.
